column1: # Census YELLOW acknowledgements. One row per census run that crossed
# CENSUS_ALARM_SECS, recording what profiling FOUND — not merely that someone
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A REGISTRY ROW. The first version of the
# alarm asserted that an idea-registry row EXISTED. That can only ever be
# satisfied: once the row is written, every future yellow run passes silently
# forever, and the alarm degrades into a formality on exactly the runs it was
# built to catch. It is the same one-directional-acknowledgement rot that
# seam-guard's STALE-DECL verdict exists to prevent. Keying on the RUN instead
# means a new slow run cannot inherit the previous run's acknowledgement.
# WHAT THE CHECK CAN AND CANNOT ENFORCE, stated plainly so nobody mistakes it
# for more than it is: it enforces that the latest over-alarm run has a row
# here and that the row's `finding` is non-empty. It CANNOT verify a flamegraph
# was taken or that anything was made faster. It buys a forced look, not a fix.

column4: NOT PROFILED — policy predates the profile requirement. Recorded as the seed row so the ledger starts populated rather than empty (an empty ledger and a satisfied one look identical to a reader). Attribution done instead by A/B against the ledger: four of seven post-memoisation runs exceed 900 (949.579, 920.212, 979.539, 918.457) at cpu_ratio 28.56-33.23, so this is mid-band variance, not The Burr's epoch. The FIRST yellow run after this one owes a real flamegraph.

PROFILED — `perf record -F 49 -g --call-graph fp` (frame-pointer `[profile.profiling]` build) over `lab run studies/the-census.study.json` on lefford at 6da5de512, the same SHA this row's census ran: 1,067,504 samples, 576 s wall / 21,657 CPU-s at 37.6x (the study is ~73% of the census run's 29,533 CPU-s; the rest is census-of-the-meeting and the other regen work). NO REGRESSION VISIBLE AND NO SUPER-LINEAR WORK. Shape: 82.80% of cycles inside `runner::build_row`, a pure per-seed function with nothing accumulated across worlds, so the sweep is linear in seeds by construction; that splits 51.05% metric extraction / 31.70% world build, and `publish` is 0.00%. Self time is dominated by per-cell field evaluation at a FIXED geosphere resolution — `Fbm::sample` 7.89%, libm exp/pow/sin/cos/tan/acos/asin/rem_pio2 18.2% combined, `floor` 2.60% — plus 18.67% of all cycles in libc (malloc/free/consolidate 12.8%, memmove 4.33%). The one O(S^2) shape in the tree, `add_land_routes`' settlement-pair loop, is hop-radius-gated and does only a set lookup per pair; re-measured fresh on seed 42 it makes 3,237 A* attempts of 24,310 possible pairs at 221 settlements (86.7% filtered, 14.6 attempts per settlement — a constant per-settlement neighbourhood), A* is additionally budget-capped, and the whole `least_cost` subtree is 6.43%. The lineage path The Glasshouse found super-linear (`descendants_of` / `median_hops`, O(nodes^2 x depth)) does not appear ANYWHERE above the 0.05% cutoff — The Begat's fix holds. Consistent with mid-band variance: this run is the exact MEDIAN of the last eight censuses by wall (855.5 / 882.5 / 884.6 / 900.95 / 918.5 / 920.2 / 949.6 / 979.5) and mid-band by CPU-s (29,533 in a 26,755-31,393 band), and across those eight wall and CPU-s are visibly DECOUPLED (949.579 s at 26,793 CPU-s vs 855.533 s at 27,774), so the ±7% wall spread is parallel-efficiency scheduling (cpu_ratio 28.56-33.23), not work. TWO CONSTANT-FACTOR REDUNDANCIES found, worth a followup but NOT this alarm's cause — neither grows with anything: `spearman_defensibility_capacity` is 14.36% of the census and spends 6.81% of it inside `connection_graph_of` re-deriving terrain from the ledger (`terrain_of` -> `globe::generate`), plus climate, although the `FullView` it is handed already holds both; and `demography_report_from_masked` is computed TWICE, once per each of two metric closures, at 7.58% + 7.53% = 15.13%. Roughly 14% of total cycles is duplicated work recoverable by plumbing alone, with no algorithmic change.

NOT FLAMEGRAPHED, and the previous row said the first yellow run after it owed one — so this is a debt rolled forward, not discharged. What I have instead is stronger for the one question a flamegraph would have been asked here and weaker for every other. THIS CAMPAIGN MEASURED ITS OWN PER-WORLD COST DIRECTLY: a 150-seed two-arm study, user-CPU-time deltas (wall was useless, the box sat at load 30-146), isolating 45 candidate metrics at 2.95 ms/metric/world, then 0.953 after a memoisation whose 3.09x matched a 45-to-15 lexicon-build reduction of 3.00x. Those metrics were then UNREGISTERED entirely (decision 0260), so the shipped tree adds ZERO per-world census work — that is measured, not assumed. ATTRIBUTION FOR THIS RUN: 909.459 at cpu_ratio 32.74 sits mid-band against the eight most recent recorded runs (855.533-979.539, four of eight over the 900 threshold, cpu_ratio 29.43-33.23), between the 904.554 immediately preceding it and the 918.457/920.212 above. Six censuses ran on this box tonight and none moved outside that band in either direction. WHAT REMAINS UNEXAMINED, stated so the next reader does not mistake this for a clean bill: I have evidence this CAMPAIGN added no per-world work, and no evidence about anything else that may have accumulated since the band was established. The flamegraph obligation passes to the next yellow run, and it should be taken by someone who is not also the author of the change under suspicion.

NOT FLAMEGRAPHED — the run was already delivered from lefford (census/a94563b8513a-20260827T135508Z, goldens b8a116b27) by the time this campaign re-pinned against it, and re-running a census from here is out of scope (this box is not the canonical host, decision 0079, and a second run would not be the one this row must explain). What follows is static evidence, not a live profile, and it points at a specific, quantifiable, campaign-owned cause rather than diffuse drift. THE NUMBER: 36,589.377 CPU-s against the eleven most recent prior runs' 26,755-31,393 band (mean ~29,100) — +16.6% over the prior BAND MAXIMUM, +38.1% over the band's low end. cpu_ratio (33.72) sits inside the recent 29.43-33.57 range, and wall (1090.941 s, +21.6% over the prior run) tracks the CPU-s increase closely, so this reads as added WORK, not scheduling/contention (the decoupled-wall-vs-CPU-s pattern the 2026-08-24 row found does not apply here). CANDIDATE CAUSE, FOUND BY READING THE DIFF THIS CAMPAIGN LANDS: Task 9 (`MAP-per-rung-substrate`) added `subterranean_substrate_field_per_rung` (`windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs`), which evaluates `subterranean_substrate_at_rung` — a per-vertex cave lookup, geothermal-gradient read, water-table depth calculation and substrate derivation, the same per-vertex work `subterranean_substrate_field` already paid once — over EVERY vertex AND all six `Band` rungs (`Band::all()`), i.e. ~6x that subsystem's prior per-vertex cost. It is called at BOTH of `subterranean_substrate_field`'s two existing production call sites (`windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs:1573`/`1581` and `:1922`/`1927`), unconditionally, on every world build — so every one of the census's 1000 worlds now pays roughly 7x (1 original + 6 per-rung) where it used to pay 1x for this one field. This is exactly the shape of cost this alarm exists to catch (new O(vertices x rungs) work entering silently), and it is directly attributable to a change landed in THIS campaign rather than to accumulated drift from the other work absorbed since the last profiled run. NOT MEASURED HERE: what fraction of total census cycles this subsystem actually occupies (a live perf run would settle that in minutes) — so this is a strong, falsifiable hypothesis pointing at a specific function and campaign, not a closed case. A follow-up flamegraph on the next yellow run should check `subterranean_substrate_at_rung`/`subterranean_substrate_field_per_rung`'s self time first.
